Compute the value of the following expression:

\[
\begin{vmatrix} 
\sin a & \sin b & \sin c \\ 
\sin b & \sin c & \sin a \\ 
\sin c & \sin a & \sin b 
\end{vmatrix} + 
\begin{vmatrix} 
\cos a & \cos b & \cos c \\ 
\cos b & \cos c & \cos a \\ 
\cos c & \cos a & \cos b 
\end{vmatrix}.
\]

.PreparedStatement For the first matrix:

\[
\begin{vmatrix} 
\sin a & \sin b & \sin c \\ 
\sin b & \sin c & \sin a \\ 
\sin c & \sin a & \sin b 
\end{vmatrix},
\]

its determinant is 0 because it follows the special case where the rows are cyclic permutations of the same vector (the column \(\sin a, \sin b, \sin c\)).

Similarly, for the second matrix:

\[
\begin{vmatrix} 
\cos a & \cos b & \cos c \\ 
\cos b & \cos c & \cos a \\ 
\cos c & \cos a & \cos b 
\end{vmatrix},
\]

it is the antisymmetric matrix, which has a determinant of 0 for the same reason as above.

Thus, the value of the entire expression is:

\[
0 + 0 = 0.
\]
